text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Shock after shock for deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller as three MPs from her party resign and she is booed at a meeting of Turkish chambers of commerce.

- Two more MPs resign from Tansu Ciller's True Path Party on Saturday, after two others resigned on Friday, heightening the struggle within the party between those for and against continuing as partners in the ruling coalition.
- Turkey's Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan is considering calling an early election without first handing over the prime minister's seat to coalition partner Tansu Ciller.
- The victory by Mohammad Khatami in Iran's presidential election indicates a swing towards liberalism and away from hard-line Islamism.
- Turkish armed forces are digging in against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels in a cross-border operation in northern Iraq.
- A week of challenges awaits the government with meetings of the Supreme Military Council, the cabinet and the National Security Council.

- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan met the military chief of staff, Ismail Hakki Karadayi on Saturday to discuss the forthcoming meeting of the Supreme Military Council and the military operation in northern Iraq.
